claims.text: The Human-Centred Personalised Admissions Framework (HCPAF) comprises five interconnected dimensions: learner profiling and contextual understanding, explainable AI decision support, equity and inclusion auditing, human oversight and shared decision-making, and personalised transition and success support.
HCPAF reconceptualises higher education admissions as the beginning of a personalised learning ecosystem rather than a terminal selection event.

In HCPAF, trust is conceptualised as a relational, calibrated, and empirically contingent mediating construct connecting transparency, fairness, learner agency, and AI adoption rather than an automatic benefit of AI adoption.
The five dimensions of HCPAF operate recursively with mutual constraints and trade-offs rather than as a frictionless linear pipeline.
HCPAF extends AI governance across the full student lifecycle via a five-stage Human-Centred AI Ecosystem spanning admissions through to graduate development.
Generative AI within HCPAF functions primarily as an interaction and explanation layer spanning Dimensions 2, 4, and 5 rather than for predictive risk estimation.

evidence.description: The framework comprises five interconnected dimensions: learner profiling and contextual understanding; explainable AI decision support; equity and inclusion auditing; human oversight and shared decision-making; and personalised transition and success support.

The Human-Centred Personalised Admissions Framework (HCPAF) reconceptualises higher education admissions as the first stage of a personalised learning ecosystem rather than a terminal selection event.

The HCPAF treats trust as a relational and contingent mediating construct rather than an automatic consequence of transparency... HCPAF consequently treats trust as an empirical outcome to be evaluated across stakeholder groups rather than as a presumed benefit of AI adoption.

The numerical ordering of the five dimensions is explanatory rather than procedural. In practice, they operate recursively... Figure 1 therefore represents the HCPAF as an interconnected system of mutual constraints and feedback rather than as a frictionless linear pipeline.

Beyond the five dimensions of HCPAF, the framework extends AI governance across the full student lifecycle through a five-stage Human-Centred AI Ecosystem. This extension recognises that admissions is not an isolated event but the beginning of an educational relationship extending through transition, learning, success, and graduate development.
Within the HCPAF, generative AI occupies a different role from predictive machine learning... GenAI is positioned mainly as an interaction and explanation layer spanning Dimensions 2, 4, and 5.

methodologies.name: Integrative literature review and conceptual synthesis
methodologies.description: An iterative and concept-led synthesis of multidisciplinary scholarship supplemented by a targeted ERIC search and bibliographic verification using publisher and policy repositories.
datasets: Policy repositories (UNESCO, OECD, EU, ICO, OfS, UCAS, Universities UK)
conditions: Peer-reviewed scholarship and policy sources published predominantly from 2012 to 2026
Inclusion based on contribution to AI/analytics capabilities, equity/privacy risks, human-centred governance theory, or regulation
Exclusion of purely technical studies disconnected from educational decision-making or learner support

methodologies.name: Human-Centred Personalised Admissions Framework (HCPAF)
methodologies.description: A five-dimensional governance architecture integrating learner profiling, explainable AI, equity auditing, human oversight, and transition support across a five-stage student lifecycle.
conditions: Human-in-the-loop oversight for all consequential decisions
Layered explanation architectures for multiple stakeholder groups

limitations.text: Evidence on prospective, live AI-assisted admissions remains limited, with most studies based on retrospective data analysis.
Much existing AI admissions scholarship is narrowly focused on prediction accuracy, enrolment optimisation, or efficiency without engaging learner agency, social inclusion, or institutional power.
The integrative literature review is concept-led rather than exhaustive, protocol-driven, or systematically reproducible, reporting no retrospective screening counts.
The HCPAF remains a conceptual framework and design heuristic rather than an empirically validated admissions model tested in live institutional deployments.
The illustrative scenarios used to demonstrate HCPAF are constructed and hypothetical rather than documented real-world implementations.

future_work.text: Empirically validate HCPAF through comparative institutional case studies examining organisational adoption, failure, and staff use or resistance to AI recommendations.
Conduct experimental studies and think-aloud protocols testing which XAI explanation formats most effectively support applicant understanding and admissions staff decision-making.

Conduct longitudinal studies testing whether connecting admissions analytics with transition support improves retention and attainment among widening participation students without increasing stigma or surveillance.
Investigate internal framework trade-offs including the balance between contextual data collection and privacy costs, and predictive performance versus explainability.
Examine equity and integrity implications of applicant generative AI use in personal statement writing using mixed methods and discourse analysis.
Execute a pre-registered systematic or scoping review to test the sensitivity of the HCPAF framework against a fully exhaustive literature corpus.
